machine: MacBook M3 Pro, home IP (Brazil), no proxy
versions: iframer-toolkit 0.10.6 (patchright, Chrome 152) · camoufox 0.5.6 / Firefox 152.0.4-beta.30 · @askjo/camofox-browser latest, same Firefox binary.
verdict: Camoufox's fingerprint claims are real. 63 detector loads across its three configs, zero flagged. iframer's best mode (headful) was flagged or partial on 6 of 21; headless on 15 of 21.
Clean fingerprint did not mean more doors open. On real walls (Cloudflare, HUMAN, Akamai, Imperva) iframer headful was the best single config: 23 of 24. Raw camoufox: 17 of 24, headless or headed.
The Hermes backend beats raw camoufox. camofox-browser (warm shared Firefox, host-matched identity) passed 41 of 45. Its only misses: Walmart, 3 of 3, and one Turnstile hiccup.

iframer headless as shipped is the weak spot: 23 of 45. The UA literally says HeadlessChrome. Everything iframer wins, it wins by escalating to a real Chrome window. On a Linux box with no display, that ladder doesn't exist, and the Hermes advice ("use camofox") is correct.

better.title: Where camoufox is better
items: Fingerprint consistency. Every property agrees with every other: UA, platform, GPU, screen, fonts. CreepJS: 6% like-headless, 0% headless, 0% stealth, every run. iframer headful: 44% like-headless, every run.
Headless that doesn't look headless. camoufox headless: 21 of 21 clean on detectors. iframer headless: 6 of 21.
No automation-protocol leaks. rebrowser's Playwright/CDP tests: 5 green every run. iframer trips viewport (default 1280×720) and useragent (Chrome for Testing brand) in every mode.
Works without a display. The whole stealth story holds in headless. That is the Hermes-on-Linux case.

better.title: Where iframer is better
items: Cloudflare challenge pages. 6 of 6 in headless and in headful. camoufox headless got stuck 2 of 6; headed 1 of 6; Hermes backend 1 of 6.

HUMAN / PerimeterX sites. Zillow: iframer 9 of 9 across modes. camoufox headed: 0 of 3 ("Press & Hold"). Walmart: iframer headful 3 of 3; camoufox headed 1 of 3, Hermes backend 0 of 3 (camoufox headless, oddly, 3 of 3).
Escalation memory. auto mode lost Ticketmaster on visit 1 (headless), remembered, and took headful on visits 2 and 3. Raw camoufox has no such ladder: a fail is a fail every time.
Real Chrome, real TLS, real engine. Some WAFs test for SpiderMonkey behaviour. camoufox's own README says it cannot hide that. iframer never has to.

method: Same machine, same network, same minute: configs interleaved per page so no engine got a quieter window.
Fresh browser and fresh cookies before every load (iframer session stop + session clear; new Camoufox() per run; new camofox userId per run).
Verdict = what the page itself said, read as text through the same JS in every engine. Parsers in targets.py, one per site, engine-blind.
iframer driven only via iframer execute --json. Camoufox only via its Python API with defaults. camofox-browser only via its REST API with defaults.
iframer auto is the product default: no --mode, so it picks, escalates, and remembers per domain (~/.iframer/domain-modes.json). Its run 2 and 3 results reflect that memory.
"unknown" = the page never rendered a verdict in the wait window. Not counted for or against anyone.
Wall time includes browser launch for raw camoufox and for iframer (browser stopped between runs); camofox-browser keeps one warm Firefox, like iframer's daemon normally does.
blank: No proxy, one IP. Every WAF also scores IP reputation; a residential IP in Brazil is a fixed variable here, not a tested one.
Behaviour. Nothing clicked, scrolled, or typed. Sites that score mouse curves and timing (HUMAN's Press & Hold, incolumitas behavioural score) were only tested on load.
Login flows and sessions. Not exercised. That is iframer's actual product surface and camoufox has nothing comparable; this benchmark is stealth-only.
Linux. Where Hermes usually runs, and where camoufox offers headless="virtual" (Xvfb). Not tested; expect camoufox to look better there, not worse.
pixelscan.net: verdict isn't in the DOM text, dropped. leboncoin.fr: CloudFront 403 for everyone (geo-block), dropped. areyouheadless: 502, dropped.
Kasada, Shape/F5, DataDome: no gradeable target in this run. DataDome was leboncoin.
Repeat visits. 3 runs is enough to see "always" vs "sometimes", not enough for a rate.

vpn.machine: same Mac, VPN exit 146.70.168.224, New York, AS9009 M247 (datacenter VPN range), 2026-09-18
verdict: Three of six sites blocked everyone, every run. g2 (Cloudflare), Ticketmaster, Indeed: 0 of 54 across all six configs. That is the IP, not the browser. No fingerprint work moves these.
On the three that still judged the browser, iframer went 26 of 27. Every mode, headless included. camoufox headless matched it, 9 of 9.
Firefox headed configs collapsed. camoufox headed 4 of 9, the Hermes backend 3 of 9. Zillow and Walmart pushed Press & Hold / Robot-or-human on them every time, and only on them.

Net: on a datacenter IP, engine choice decides 3 sites and the IP decides the other 3. iframer and camoufox headless tie on the ones that are decidable; the Hermes setup as shipped is the worst row here.

docker.machine: Docker Desktop on the same Mac, home IP, arm64 Linux containers (a real VPS would be x86_64), no GPU, 2026-09-18
verdict: In a container, camoufox headless is the best config and it isn't close. Detectors 21 of 21, real sites 13 of 18. iframer's best (headful over Xvfb): 14 of 21 and 7 of 14, with 4 more runs that never returned.

Cloudflare's challenge pages blocked every container config, 0 of 36, on the same home IP where iframer on the Mac went 6 of 6. Diagnosed after the run: egress IP identical, challenge script loads and posts its fingerprint fine, 60 s wait changes nothing, and an x86_64 container under Rosetta fails the same way, so it is not arm64. What's left is what every container here shares: no GPU (software canvas, no WebGL in headless) and Docker Desktop's user-space network stack, whose TCP fingerprint is the Mac's while the browser claims Linux or Windows. Treat this row as a Docker-Desktop-on-Mac finding until a real Linux host is tested.

iframer's Docker mode has three bugs before stealth even matters. The server binds 127.0.0.1 so the shipped compose file is unreachable from the host; the daemon reaps its own Chrome because the pid-1 liveness check fails in a container (worked around with --init); and 14 of 144 iframer runs hung until the container was restarted.

The leaks are the same ones as on the Mac, plus one. Headless: HeadlessChrome UA, Linux UA with Win32 platform. Headful: Windows UA on a Linux box with an Intel Iris GPU string and a 1280×720 screen. Same generator, same seams.
Firefox with a window loses to HUMAN here too. camoufox virtual (Xvfb) and the Hermes backend: Zillow 0 of 3 each, Walmart 0 to 1 of 3. camoufox plain headless: Zillow 3 of 3.
